claims.text: Compositional complexity forms and stabilizes the protective oxide layer in high-entropy alloys.
Compositional complexity promotes simultaneous oxidation of multiple constituent elements.
Sluggish diffusion kinetics produce a continuous, multicomponent, adherent oxide film.
The starting alloy is a homogenized solid solution with a random distribution of multiple principal elements.
The alloy develops a continuous and compositionally graded multicomponent oxide layer during high-temperature oxidation.
The oxide layer resists further oxidation because it is adherent.
The oxide layer resists further oxidation because it has low diffusivity for oxygen and metal ions.
The multicomponent alloy makeup causes sluggish diffusion among cation species.
Sluggish cation diffusion leads to synchronous oxidation of several elements.
Synchronous oxidation of several elements forms a mixed oxide scale.
The mixed oxide scale is more uniform than scales formed on simpler alloys.
The mixed oxide scale is more adherent than scales formed on simpler alloys.
The onset and rate of protective oxide formation correlate with slowed ionic diffusion and oxide-phase stability.
Oxidation in air at 900–1100°C will produce multiple oxide phases detectable by HTXRD.
The high-entropy alloy will exhibit less oxidation penetration than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The high-entropy alloy will exhibit slower oxidation kinetics than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Vacuum treatment will result in negligible or no oxidation.
The proposed behavior applies at approximately 900–1100°C to alloys with significant compositional complexity and may not occur at lower temperatures or in less compositionally complex alloys.

contradictions.description: Vacuum is described as producing negligible or no oxidation, but the falsification rule requires the air-oxidized high-entropy alloy to have slower oxidation kinetics than the vacuum-treated sample. An oxidizing exposure cannot meaningfully demonstrate slower oxidation than a no-oxidation vacuum control.
